page: Microsoft Azure E16as_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the AMD EPYC 7763 processor on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The x86_64 architecture provides 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading at clock speeds up to 3.525 GHz. Memory allocation totals 128.0 GB of RAM, maintaining an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio. The processor integrates 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, with hardware instruction support for AVX, AES, VAES, SHA-NI, and BMI2, while omitting AVX-512 extensions. The instance includes no local storage and no bundled GPUs, requiring remote network storage such as Azure Premium Storage.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-core compute performance, with stress-ng reaching 2703.19, placing it in the upper quartile. Multi-core compute performance remains balanced within median tiers, recording 21581.29 on stress-ng and 9104.0 on Geekbench multi-core. In memory subsystems, cached read throughput achieves 1030.61 GB/sec, while uncached large-block reads reach 39.93 GB/sec. However, uncached large-block write operations register at 25.1 GB/sec, placing memory write throughput in the lower quartile.

In operational testing, the instance logged 15.94 million operations per second in Redis SET workloads, a PassMark database score of 6769.16, and static web serving throughput of 16.89 GB/sec. Small 135M language model prompt processing achieved 929.72 tokens per second, while 7B parameter models reached 9.5 tokens per second for generation. Given the 8:1 RAM-to-vCPU density and absence of local disks, the E16as_v5 offers cost-efficient scaling for in-memory databases, memory-bound caching systems, enterprise application backends, and data analytics tasks relying on network-attached storage.
description: Microsoft Azure E16as_v5 is a memory-optimized cloud server built on the AMD EPYC 7763 processor using the x86_64 architecture. It provides 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores alongside 128.0 GB of system memory, delivering an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio. The configuration contains no onboard local storage and operates without hardware accelerators, utilizing remote storage volumes for persistent data. Synthetic benchmarks show strong single-core CPU execution alongside median-tier multi-core and database processing scores, while uncached memory write bandwidth exhibits lower performance relative to peer hardware classes. Real-world evaluation highlights solid memory operations, achieving 15.94 million Redis SET operations per second and 16.89 GB/sec static web throughput. The instance is structured to deliver resource efficiency for memory-intensive enterprise workloads, including in-memory caching platforms, mid-sized relational databases, analytics engines, and transactional backend servers relying on external managed block storage.
